symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G=(V,E^{\to},E^{\leftrightarrow})\)

symbols.name: Gplus
symbols.def: \(G^{+}\) expands every physically addressable edge mechanism and mediator of \(G\)

symbols.name: A
symbols.space: explicit SELECT, RAND, CTF-RAND, and READ records
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A\) stores each action's type, endpoints, affected child set, allowed values, prerequisites, conflicts, ownership, and canonical topological position in \(G^{+}\)

symbols.name: Qord
symbols.def: \(Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)=P_{\operatorname{do}(V\setminus S_0=x_0)}(S_0=s_0)\)

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=P(\mathbf Y_{\ast}=\mathbf y)\)

symbols.name: Dord
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}=(G,S_0,x_0,(\kappa_v)_{v\in V})\) is an additive-cost instance whose target is the ordinary kernel \(Q[S_0](\cdot;x_0)\).

symbols.name: DordClass
symbols.type: finite class of ordinary query-design instances
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\) is the ordinary \(Q[S]\) subclass in Definition \(\mathrm{Ordinary\ query\ subclass}\).
symbols.role: domain of the two-way ordinary embedding

symbols.name: Bord
symbols.def: \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\) is an ordinary identifying collection for \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\)

symbols.name: Wstar
symbols.def: \(\mathbf W_{\ast}\) is obtained from \(Q\) by counterfactual ancestor expansion and the ancestral-set transformation

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: \(k\) is the number of bidirected districts in \(G[V(\mathbf W_{\ast})]\)

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: \((C_1,\ldots,C_k)\) is the district factorization of \(\mathbf W_{\ast}\)

symbols.name: Cj
symbols.def: \(C_j\) is the \(j\)-th component of \(C\)

symbols.name: Osrc
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) returns an immutable symbolic handle for the complete acquired law of a queried protocol and its exact finite support table over recorded action labels and READ outputs.

symbols.name: Reg
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Reg}(S)=h_S\) and its support is \(\operatorname{supp}_S\) when \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)=(h_S,\operatorname{supp}_S)\); it is undefined when the oracle returns \(\bot\).

symbols.name: LIT
symbols.space: canonically indexed action-assignment and factor-request literals
symbols.def: \(\mathrm{LIT}=\{(a,x):a\in\mathcal A,\ x\text{ is an allowed value recorded for }a\}\sqcup\{(j,v,x):j\in[k],\ v\text{ occurs in the transformed ancestry requested by }C_j,\ x\in\mathfrak X_v\}\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{k}\{j\}\times\Omega_j\), where \(\Omega_j\) contains every complete assignment of the free transformed-ancestry request positions of \(C_j\), paired with its induced equality type.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \(\ell\) is the canonical \( |\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit incidence vector of a consistent set of action assignments, conditioned READ values, and factor requests; it selects at most one value for each indexed action or READ endpoint.

symbols.name: Hslice
symbols.def: \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) is the admissible conditioning event defined by the asserted RAND, CTF-RAND, and READ-value literals in \(\ell\).

symbols.name: Qfam
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}=\{Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}=\{P_b(V\setminus B_i):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\).

symbols.name: LambdaB
symbols.def: \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}=\{\ell_{i,b}:i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\), where \(\ell_{i,b}\) records RAND assignment \(b\) and the complete READ mask on \(V\)
symbols.role: ordinary embedding label and slice data

symbols.name: Tsource
symbols.def: \(T\) is a single-district source factor extracted from \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\)

symbols.name: Transcript
symbols.space: ancestor sets, retained districts, and literal-match checks

symbols.name: Ebase
symbols.def: \(E_0\) is a finite lexicographically ordered list of protocol, slice-label, and labelled-source masks, without branch-ownership or restriction-transcript fields.
symbols.role: generic fixed source acquisition supplied to complete CTFIDU\({}^{+}\)

symbols.name: Ecert
symbols.space: protocol bits, literal bits, factor-ownership bits, source masks, and restriction transcripts

symbols.name: EB
symbols.def: \(E_{\mathbf B}\) is the canonical SELECT-RAND-READ certificate constructed from \(\mathbf B\) and \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}\)

symbols.name: Rec
symbols.def: \(R=(b_S,b_{\ell},b_J,b_T,(\tau_j)_{j\in J})\), with fixed-width masks over \(\mathcal A\), \(\mathrm{LIT}\), \([k]\), and \(V\sqcup(V\times\mathrm{LIT})\).

symbols.name: Rsrc
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R(E_0)\), or \(\mathcal R(E)\), is the deduplicated lexicographic list of protocol-slice-source triples decoded from the generic acquired collection or uniform certificate.

symbols.name: Nsrc
symbols.def: \(N_{\mathrm{src}}\) is the exact bit length of \(\mathcal R(E_0)\) or \(\mathcal R(E)\) under the source-collection encoding.

symbols.name: Nenc
symbols.def: \(N_E=\sum_{R\in E}\bigl(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)+\sum_{j\in J(R)}|\operatorname{enc}(\tau_j)|\bigr)\).

symbols.name: Phys
symbols.type: finite structural string with oracle access
symbols.def: \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}=(x_{\mathrm{str}},\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}})\) is the certificate-independent structural encoding and the explicitly charged source-law/support interface in Definition \(\mathrm{Physical\ input\ interface}\).

symbols.name: Nin
symbols.def: \(N_{\mathrm{in}}=|x_{\mathrm{str}}|=|\operatorname{enc}(G^{+})|+|\operatorname{enc}(\{\mathfrak X_v\}_{v\in V})|+|\operatorname{enc}(\mathcal A)|+\operatorname{bitlen}(c)+|\operatorname{enc}(Q,C,\mathrm{LIT})|+|\operatorname{enc}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\text{ signature})|\).

symbols.name: Noracle
symbols.def: \(N_{\mathcal O}\) is the sum of the bit lengths of all protocol queries and all returned law handles, support-index headers, and support bit tables in one verifier or optimization execution.

symbols.name: Bcert
symbols.def: \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}=k\bigl(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)\bigr)+8k(|V|+1)^2\lceil\log_2(|V|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+2)\rceil\).

symbols.name: Acc
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)\) is the parse, legality, source-typing, complete-run, and transcript-verification predicate in Definition \(\mathrm{Operational\ acceptance}\).

symbols.name: Estar
symbols.def: \(E^{\star}\) is the lexicographically first minimum-cost accepting canonical certificate when one exists.

symbols.name: NEstar
symbols.def: \(N_{E^{\star}}\) is the exact encoding length \(N_E\) evaluated at \(E=E^{\star}\).

symbols.name: Opt
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Opt}=\inf\{\operatorname{Cost}(E):\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\)

symbols.name: Hnorm
symbols.def: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{norm}}\) follows the published ancestor-district recursion with symbolic literals, proves invariance across the finite branch set \(\Omega\), and keeps the chosen source outside the universal assignment-and-equality-type quantifier.

symbols.name: Hsearch
symbols.def: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{search}}\) combines memoized enumeration of distinct protocol support replies with an adversarial oracle decision tree indexed by unresolved factor-source incidences.

symbols.name: Asep
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sep}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\)

symbols.name: Sind
symbols.def: \(S_{\mathrm{ind}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\)

symbols.def: \(S_{\mathrm{dir}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\)

assumptions.condition: \(G\) is a finite ADMG induced by a recursive finite-discrete SCM.
\(|\mathfrak X_v|\le d\) for every observed variable \(v\in V\).
\(Q\) belongs to the physically realizable Layer-2.5 query language over \(G\).

For every record \(R\in E\) with nonempty factor-ownership mask that decodes to \(S\in\Pi\) and \(\ell\), the support table returned by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) assigns positive mass to \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\).

novel.justification: This is a physical Layer-2.5 slice-positivity restriction. It is realized by a finite-state digital experimentation platform that SELECTs from positive-mass enrollment strata, routes every catalogued RAND and CTF-RAND value with positive probability, and exposes a source record only when the complete conjunction of its asserted READ values is a predeclared positive-mass logged cell under that route. It excludes unsupported conjunctions of randomized labels and recorded values without imposing positivity on unused cells or on events that cannot be formed from the protocol record.

assumptions.condition: Each \(a\in\mathcal A\) has exactly one type in \(\{\mathrm{SELECT},\mathrm{RAND},\mathrm{CTF\text{-}RAND},\mathrm{READ}\}\) and explicit endpoints, affected children, allowed values, prerequisites, conflicts, and ownership data.

novel.justification: Laboratory protocols and platform experiments are routinely specified by executable actions, admissible settings, device conflicts, and measurement endpoints; the catalogue records these operational constraints without positing an unobservable causal functional.

assumptions.condition: \(c(a)\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}\) is encoded in binary for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).

novel.justification: Fixed monetary or resource charges for laboratory actions are naturally nonnegative and finitely recorded; binary rational encoding permits heterogeneous costs without a unary-magnitude convention.

assumptions.condition: The SELECT action in \(S\) draws a fresh unit independently from the target population.

novel.justification: Exact independent superpopulation sampling is an idealized platform assumption, realized when each protocol execution enrolls one unit by independent sampling with replacement from a target-population frame or draws a newly generated unit from a stable production process. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025) instead define SELECT as sampling units without replacement, so their ICLR result does not justify the exact independence condition imposed here.

assumptions.condition: Along \(S\), each physical mechanism represented in \(G^{+}\) is executed at most once on the selected unit.
If \(a\in S\) and \(b\) precedes \(a\) in the catalogue, then \(b\in S\) and \(b\) occurs before \(a\) in canonical order.

novel.justification: Physical data acquisition commonly requires setup actions before randomization and measurement, such as enrollment before treatment and treatment before outcome READ.

assumptions.condition: No pair of catalogue actions linked by the conflict relation is jointly contained in \(S\).

novel.justification: Mutually exclusive devices, incompatible assay choices, and alternative randomization modes are ordinary features of executable experimental protocols.

assumptions.condition: Whenever \(\ell\) asserts an action assignment \((a,x)\) for \(a\in S\), the value \(x\) belongs to the catalogued allowed-value set of \(a\).

novel.justification: Intervention devices and experimental policies often permit only a specified finite menu of doses, messages, or attribute values.

assumptions.condition: The ordered actions in \(S\) satisfy the simultaneous potential-response compatibility criterion of CTF-REALIZE on \(G^{+}\).
Every optional purchasable protocol \(S\in\Pi\) contains exactly one action \(a\) with \(c(a)>0\).

novel.justification: This restricted physical subclass is realized when every menu option shares zero-cost enrollment and readout infrastructure but activates exactly one billable assay, actuator, or treatment-delivery module. The restriction concerns the platform cost architecture and is not imposed on the general acquisition problem.

assumptions.condition: Legality of each optional protocol \(S\in\Pi\) is invariant to which other protocols are acquired on distinct fresh units.

novel.justification: This restricted physical subclass is realized by isolated fresh-unit runs with separately reserved devices and no cross-run capacity, contamination, or interference constraints. It is a substantive platform restriction and is not inferred from ordinary intervention semantics.

assumptions.condition: Each target factor \(C_j\) is certified by one acquired protocol independently of the presence of other acquired protocols.

novel.justification: This restricted physical subclass is realized by a registry in which each reported target factor must be certified from one independently audited assay channel and combining distinct protocol reports cannot create a new certificate. It deliberately excludes multi-source identification synergy and is not imposed on the general acquisition problem.

assumptions.condition: For every source factor extracted from \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\), each counterfactual ancestor required by the ancestral-set transformation is either an endpoint of a READ action in \(S\) or has its value fixed by an action recorded in \(S\).

novel.justification: A realizable platform regime is a digital experiment in which SELECT enrolls a fresh account, RAND or CTF-RAND records the delivered treatment on each affected edge, and READ logs every natural covariate, mediator, and outcome in the requested factor's transformed ancestry; action-fixed vertices need no duplicate natural-value measurement. The restriction excludes a READ of \(Y\) alone in \(X\to Y\) when natural \(X\) is required, and excludes any factor whose natural parent or mediator is privacy-redacted and not fixed. It permits omission only of variables outside the required transformed ancestry or variables whose relevant value is explicitly fixed by the recorded protocol.

definitions.name: Certificate-independent physical input and source interface \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\)
definitions.construction: The structural string \(x_{\mathrm{str}}\) self-delimits the vertex and domain tables; the directed and bidirected edges of \(G^{+}\); every action type, endpoint, affected-child list, allowed-value list, precedence edge, conflict edge, ownership endpoint, and binary-rational cost in \((\mathcal A,c)\); and the unnested query \(Q\), transformed ancestry, ordered factors \(C\), and canonical literal table \(\mathrm{LIT}\). Independently of every certificate, the instance supplies oracle access to \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\). A query is exactly an \(|\mathcal A|\)-bit protocol mask \(S\). The answer is either \(\bot\), or an immutable symbolic handle \(h_S\) for the complete acquired law followed by a self-delimiting support bit table indexed lexicographically by the Cartesian product of the catalogued allowed-value lists of the RAND and CTF-RAND actions in \(S\) and the encoded domains of the READ endpoints in \(S\); its exact payload is one bit per element of that product plus the handle and index headers. The table therefore decides the support of every admissible event and every READ cell exactly; CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) manipulates \(h_S\) symbolically and never evaluates a hidden law. One execution is charged \(N_{\mathcal O}\), the total bits in its oracle queries and replies, and may cache one reply per distinct protocol. The finite structural length is \(N_{\mathrm{in}}=|x_{\mathrm{str}}|\). No protocol choice, slice label, source mask, factor-ownership choice, transcript, oracle reply, or source-law value occurs in \(x_{\mathrm{str}}\).

definitions.name: Structural target-factor tuple \(C\)
definitions.construction: Apply counterfactual ancestor expansion and the ancestral-set transformation to \(Q\), then partition \(\mathbf W_{\ast}\) into the ordered bidirected districts \(C=(C_1,\ldots,C_k)\) of \(G[V(\mathbf W_{\ast})]\).

definitions.name: Legal protocol class \(\Pi(G^{+},\mathcal A)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Pi(G^{+},\mathcal A)=\{S\subseteq\mathcal A: |S\cap\mathrm{SELECT}|=1,\ S\text{ selects a fresh independent unit},\ S\text{ uses each mechanism at most once},\ S\text{ is precedence closed and conflict free, and }S\text{ satisfies CTF\text{-}REALIZE on }G^{+}\}\).

definitions.name: Acquired regime \(\operatorname{Reg}(S)\)
definitions.construction: For \(S\in\Pi\), query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) once. If the reply is \((h_S,\operatorname{supp}_S)\), define \(\operatorname{Reg}(S)=h_S\) with the returned exact support over its recorded assignment labels and READ outputs; if the reply is \(\bot\), \(\operatorname{Reg}(S)\) is unavailable. Repeated slices of one protocol reuse the cached handle and support table.

definitions.name: Canonical literal and label encoding
definitions.construction: Order \(\mathrm{LIT}\) lexicographically after forming the disjoint union of action-value literals \(\{(a,x):a\in\mathcal A,\ x\text{ is catalogued for }a\}\) and request literals \(\{(j,v,x):j\in[k],\ v\text{ occurs in the transformed ancestry requested by }C_j,\ x\in\mathfrak X_v\}\). Thus \( |\mathrm{LIT}|\le d\bigl(|\mathcal A|+\sum_{j=1}^{k}|\{v:v\text{ occurs in that transformed ancestry of }C_j\}|\bigr)\), and every \(\ell\) is represented by exactly \( |\mathrm{LIT}|\) bits. Reject a label if it asserts two values for one indexed endpoint, mentions a literal absent from \(\mathrm{LIT}\), or assigns a value not allowed by the catalogue.

definitions.name: Admissible physical source event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\)
definitions.construction: For \(S\in\Pi\) and a consistent \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit label \(\ell\), \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) is defined exactly when every asserted action-value literal \((a,x)\) names a RAND or CTF-RAND action \(a\in S\) at a catalogued value, every asserted request literal \((j,v,x)\) names an endpoint \(v\) READ by \(S\) that occurs in the transformed ancestry requested by \(C_j\), no indexed action or READ endpoint receives two values, and no other or unrecorded equality is imposed. When defined, it is the event that every asserted action records its asserted value and every asserted READ endpoint equals its asserted value.

definitions.name: Measured source slice \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\)
definitions.construction: For a legal \(S\) with oracle reply \((h_S,\operatorname{supp}_S)\) and a consistent \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit label \(\ell\), \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\) is the symbolic READ projection of \(h_S\) conditioned on \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\). It is defined exactly when the returned support table gives that event positive mass. Extraction returns no source factor unless every counterfactual ancestor required by its ancestral-set transformation is READ by \(S\) or fixed by a recorded action in \(S\).

definitions.name: Value-matching dependency graph \(D_{T}\)
definitions.construction: For a labelled source factor \(T\), let \(D_T\) have vertex set \(T\) and arc \(u\to v\) exactly when \(u\to v\) is directed in \(G\) and the value carried by the source literal for \(u\) equals the value requested for \(u\) in the parent subscript of \(v\); on \(U\subseteq T\), use the induced digraph \(D_T[U]\).

definitions.name: Connected-ancestor obstruction family \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)=\{F: C_j\subsetneq F\subseteq T,\ G^{\leftrightarrow}[F]\text{ is connected, and every }v\in F\text{ reaches some }c\in C_j\text{ in }D_T[F]\}\).

definitions.name: Restriction transcript \(\tau_j\)
definitions.construction: \(\tau_j=((U_0,H_0,B_0),\ldots,(U_m,H_m,B_m))\) records the chosen source \(U_0=T\), each value-matching ancestor set \(H_r=\operatorname{An}_{C_j}(D_T[U_r])\), and the retained bidirected district \(B_r\) containing \(C_j\), terminating with \(H_m=C_j\).

definitions.name: Finite uniform protocol-slice record \(R\)
definitions.construction: A record is \(R=(b_S,b_{\ell},b_J,b_T,(\tau_j)_{j\in J})\), where \(b_S\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathcal A|}\) is a protocol mask, \(b_{\ell}\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathrm{LIT}|}\) is its slice label, \(b_J\in\{0,1\}^{k}\) owns target factors, and \(b_T\in\{0,1\}^{V\sqcup(V\times\mathrm{LIT})}\) records the labelled single-district source factor extracted from that slice. Its fixed-width part has \(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)\) bits, followed by self-delimiting encodings of one transcript schema per owned factor.

definitions.name: Uniform acquisition certificate \(E\)
definitions.construction: \(E\) is a lexicographically ordered finite list of uniform records. After empty ownership masks are discarded, the nonempty factor masks \(J\) partition \([k]\). Each decoded \(S\) lies in \(\Pi\); \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) returns a law handle and support table; each decoded \(\ell\) names a positive well-typed slice; and \(b_T\) names one extracted source factor. For every owned \(C_j\), the same selected protocol, slice, source, and transcript schema succeeds for every branch in \(\Omega_j\), so source choice is outside the assignment-and-equality-type quantifier. Records sharing a protocol pay its cost once. The exact certificate length is \(N_E=\sum_{R\in E}\bigl(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)+\sum_{j\in J(R)}|\operatorname{enc}(\tau_j)|\bigr)\).

definitions.name: Complete-run source collection \(\mathcal R(E)\)
definitions.construction: From either a generic acquired collection \(E_0\) or a uniform certificate \(E\), retain one copy of each distinct triple consisting of its protocol mask, label mask, and labelled-source mask, and sort the triples lexicographically. The protocol, label, and source masks have lengths \(|\mathcal A|\), \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)\), respectively, so the exact input length is \(N_{\mathrm{src}}=|\mathcal R(E_0)|\bigl(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)\bigr)\), or the same expression with \(E\).

definitions.name: Distinct-protocol cost \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)\)
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)=\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_0)}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)\) for a generic acquired collection, and identically with \(E\) for a uniform certificate, where \(\operatorname{Prot}\) contains each distinct acquired protocol mask once irrespective of its number of slices, sources, or factors.

definitions.name: Operational acceptance \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)\)
definitions.construction: Parse the finite structural string \(x_{\mathrm{str}}\) before reading the supplied finite certificate string \(E\). Parse \(E\) into the fixed-width masks and self-delimiting transcripts of the uniform-record definition. Return \(0\) for malformed input, malformed certificate length or identifier, repeated record, nonpartition of \([k]\), illegal protocol, inconsistent or out-of-catalogue label, oracle reply \(\bot\), malformed oracle support index, undefined event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\), zero support for that event, source mask not extracted from the returned law handle, failed measured-ancestry typing, or invalid restriction step. Otherwise cache the oracle reply for each distinct protocol, construct the entire deduplicated source collection \(\mathcal R(E)\), normalize \(Q\), and execute complete unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) from the first ancestral-set transformation through factorization and exhaustive search over every decoded source. Return \(1\) exactly when the complete run does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), every \(C_j\) is owned exactly once, and each claimed protocol, slice, source, and transcript schema reproduces a successful IDENTIFY\({}^{+}\) branch for every assignment and induced equality type in \(\Omega_j\). Return \(0\) otherwise. Every source-law or support access is an explicit \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) query charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\); \(\operatorname{Reg}\) contains no hidden law or positivity test.

definitions.name: Optimal acquisition cost \(\operatorname{Opt}\)
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Opt}=\inf\{\operatorname{Cost}(E): E\text{ is a uniform acquisition certificate and }\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).

definitions.name: Uniform-normalization handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{norm}}\)
definitions.construction: Run the published IDENTIFY\({}^{+}\) ancestor-district recursion with symbolic request literals, partition the finite valuations only by induced equality type, and prove that a successful selected source and restriction path persist under every refinement of those symbolic values. The selected source remains outside the universal quantifier over \(\Omega_j\).

definitions.name: Oracle-search handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{search}}\)
definitions.construction: Memoize the reply to each queried protocol, branch first on the unresolved factor-source incidence with the fewest legal protocols, and pair the resulting upper-bound algorithm with an adversarial pair of source oracles that agree on every queried protocol until a decisive support cell is exposed.

definitions.name: Ordinary \(Q[S]\) query subclass \(\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}=\{\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}=(G,S_0,x_0,(\kappa_v)_{v\in V}):G\text{ is a finite semi-Markovian ADMG},\ \varnothing\ne S_0\subseteq V,\ x_0\in\mathfrak X_{V\setminus S_0},\ \kappa_v\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0},\text{ and the target is }Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)=P_{\operatorname{do}(V\setminus S_0=x_0)}(S_0=s_0)\}\).

definitions.name: Layer-2.5 translation of an ordinary \(Q[S]\) query
definitions.construction: Translate \(Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)\) to the single-world unnested Layer-2.5 event \(Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0)\). Translate each ordinary input kernel \(Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b)\) to the labelled slice law \(P_b(V\setminus B)\); no cross-world variable is introduced by this translation.

definitions.name: Ordinary \(Q[S]\) source family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\)
definitions.construction: For \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\), set \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}=\{Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}=\{P_b(V\setminus B_i):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\). The collection \(\mathbf B\) is ordinary identifying exactly when the ordinary ID procedure identifies \(Q[S_0](\cdot;x_0)\) from this full finite source family.

definitions.name: Ordinary-design embedding \(\iota\) on \(\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\)
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}=(G,S_0,x_0,(\kappa_v)_{v\in V})\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\), set the Layer-2.5 target to \(Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0)\) and let \(G^{+}\) retain the ordinary node mechanisms. The catalogue has one mandatory fresh-unit SELECT \(s\) with \(c(s)=0\); for every \(v\in V\), one RAND action \(r_v\) that draws independently and uniformly from \(\mathfrak X_v\), affects exactly the ordinary children of \(v\), and costs \(c(r_v)=\kappa_v\); and one READ action \(\rho_v\) with endpoint \(v\) and cost zero. SELECT precedes every other action, remaining actions follow canonical causal order, and there are no conflicts or CTF-RAND actions. For \(B\subseteq V\), let \(S_B=\{s\}\cup\{r_v:v\in B\}\cup\{\rho_v:v\in V\}\). Conditioning its independent RAND labels at \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\) produces the Layer-2.5 translation of the ordinary source \(Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B)\), with positive label probability and protocol cost \(\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\). The source interface returns for each \(S_B\) an immutable handle for this complete ordinary experimental law and its exact support table; because each RAND coordinate is uniform, every assignment-label event has positive support. Oracle answers for protocols outside the SELECT-RAND-READ image are irrelevant to the embedding.

definitions.name: Finite ordinary label and slice data \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}\)
definitions.construction: For every \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\), set \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}=\{\ell_{i,b}:i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\). The label \(\ell_{i,b}\) is the exact \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit vector assigning each RAND action \(r_v\in S_{B_i}\) the coordinate \(b_v\) and all unconditioned literal bits zero. The protocol contains the adequate READ set \(\{\rho_v:v\in V\}\), and \(\operatorname{Slice}(S_{B_i},\ell_{i,b})=Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B_i)\). The family has exactly \(\sum_{i=1}^{t}\prod_{v\in B_i}|\mathfrak X_v|\) labelled slices before duplicate intervention sets are coalesced.

definitions.name: Canonical embedded certificate \(E_{\mathbf B}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\) be any ordinary identifying collection for an instance in \(\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\). Acquire exactly one SELECT-RAND-READ protocol \(S_B\) for each distinct \(B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}\) and all labels in \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}\). For every such \((B,b)\) and every canonically ordered labelled single-district factor of \(Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B)\), include its protocol, label, and source masks. For each target factor \(C_j\), assign ownership to the lexicographically first included ordinary source and finite ancestor-district transcript schema that succeed uniformly over \(\Omega_j\), as guaranteed by the uniform-source theorem. Retain an empty-ownership record when needed to preserve each distinct paid protocol, merge equal records, and sort lexicographically. The resulting finite uniform certificate is \(E_{\mathbf B}\).

definitions.name: Positive binary separation models and catalogue
definitions.construction: In each model let \(U_X,U_A,U_B,U_C\) be mutually independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) bits and let \(E_Y,E_Z\) be mutually independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)\) bits independent of them. Model \(M_1\) has \(X=U_X\), \(Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_B)\oplus E_Y\), and \(Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_C)\oplus E_Z\). Model \(M_2\) has \(X=U_X\), \(Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_C)\oplus E_Y\), and \(Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_A)\oplus E_Z\). The catalogue is \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sep}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\): \(s\) is a fresh SELECT; \(\chi_{Y,0}\) is CTF-RAND transmitting value zero from \(X\) only to child \(Y\); \(\chi_{Z,1}\) transmits value one only to child \(Z\); and \(\rho_v\) READs \(v\). SELECT precedes both CTF-RAND actions, which precede the READs; there are no conflicts. Set \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Y,0})=c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Z,1})=1\) and all other costs to zero. For each displayed legal protocol, \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) returns the law generated by the displayed SCM equations and the exact binary support table; independent response noise makes every READ cell compatible with a fixed RAND or CTF-RAND label positive.

definitions.name: One-action no-synergy subclass \(\mathfrak C_{1}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_{1}=\{(G^{+},\mathcal A,Q):\text{every optional }S\in\Pi\text{ has exactly one positive-cost action, protocol legality is invariant across distinct fresh-unit acquisitions, and each }C_j\text{ is certified by one protocol without cross-protocol synergy}\}\).

statements.statement: Fix a labelled source factor \(T\) and nonempty target factor \(C_j\subseteq T\), with each observable variable appearing at most once and both \(G^{\leftrightarrow}[T]\) and \(G^{\leftrightarrow}[C_j]\) connected. Then \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}(G,C_j,T)=\operatorname{FAIL}\) if and only if \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)\neq\varnothing\).
statements.justification: This static iff obstruction is the local mathematical object needed to replace an opaque recursive failure trace.
statements.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026), Lemmas 3.3--3.4, characterize failure through a ctf-hedge detected by recursion; they do not state the restriction-invariant connected-ancestor iff form.
statements.consumer: The relational compiler uses the obstruction formula without materializing transitive closure or enumerating protocols.

statements.statement: When \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)=\varnothing\), the successful restriction transcript \(\tau_j\) has at most \(|T|\) strict restriction steps and admits an \(O(|T|^2)\)-bit representation apart from literal identifiers; each step is verifiable by graph traversal and value comparison.
statements.justification: Polynomial local transcripts are required for an explicit certificate output rather than a black-box acceptance bit.
statements.gap: The published algorithm terminates, but no acquisition-oriented transcript-size statement is given for value-labelled source restrictions.
statements.consumer: A verifier can audit each selected source use and reconstruct the symbolic factor identification path.

statements.statement: For every finite acquired collection \(E_0\) on which the full correctly typed unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))\) procedure accepts, there exists a uniform certificate \(E\) using only protocols and slices represented in \(E_0\), with \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)\le\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\), at most one source-slice record per target factor \(C_j\), at most \(k\) nonempty records, and at most \(k\) distinct protocols. For each factor, its selected protocol, slice, labelled source, and ancestor-district transcript schema succeed simultaneously for every assignment and induced equality type in \(\Omega_j\). Conversely, every uniform certificate accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) induces a complete accepting CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) run on \(\mathcal R(E)\).
statements.justification: This quantifier-exchange theorem is the load-bearing bridge from complete fixed-source identification to a compact acquisition certificate and is directly stress-tested by the finite equality-type search.
statements.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026), Algorithm 2 and Appendix E, establish completeness for concrete labelled queries and fixed regimes; they do not prove that one selected source and restriction schema remain valid across every free assignment and equality type of a target factor.
statements.consumer: The theorem limits paid acquisitions and auditable source transcripts by the number of target districts rather than the number of value assignments.

statements.statement: Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\). If the oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\) is feasible, then it has a lexicographically canonical accepting uniform certificate with at most \(k\) nonempty records, one owned transcript schema for each factor, no empty-ownership record, and no larger cost than any accepting acquired collection. Every transcript has at most \(n\) strict restrictions and at most \(8(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\) bits. Consequently \(N_E\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}=k(m+L+k+n(1+L))+8k(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\le8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4\). Thus the lexicographically first optimum \(E^{\star}\) exists and its certificate length is polynomial in the structural input and \(k\); oracle replies are separately charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).
statements.justification: The bound separates compact existential certificate data from potentially large, explicitly charged oracle support replies.
statements.gap: Fixed-source completeness provides no canonical polynomial bound on an endogenous physical acquisition certificate or its transcript schema.
statements.consumer: The exact optimizer can bound certificate enumeration while reporting source-interface cost separately.

statements.statement: Determine whether exact minimum-cost uniform-certificate optimization under the unrestricted charged source interface can use \(2^{O(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time and oracle-answer space, or whether an adversarial pair of finite support oracles forces \(2^{\Omega(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\) certificate or protocol queries even when \(k\) and \(d\) are fixed.
statements.justification: The source interface makes exact optimization well posed but leaves a sharp oracle-complexity frontier between memoized search and information-theoretic lower bounds.
statements.gap: Neither fixed-source CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) nor ordinary intervention-design algorithms analyze the query complexity of discovering support-bearing physical protocols through an explicit law oracle.
statements.consumer: A positive algorithm would make the certified planner usable on large catalogues, while a lower bound would identify which finite support representation must be added before reviving a treewidth method.

statements.statement: If the independently specified oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}=(x_{\mathrm{str}},\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}})\) is feasible, then the minimum defining \(\operatorname{Opt}\) is attained by the lexicographically first canonical uniform certificate \(E^{\star}\). Exhaustive enumeration of certificates of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), with cached oracle replies, outputs \(E^{\star}\), its protocol masks, exact \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit slice labels, source masks, factor-ownership masks, and one uniform finite restriction transcript schema per factor. Its time is \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{E^{\star}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), where \(N_{\mathcal O}\) charges every issued protocol query and returned law-handle and support-table bit. The verifier executes complete unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) on the decoded oracle-backed source collection. No bounded-treewidth runtime is claimed.
statements.justification: The theorem retains exact cost optimization while exposing both the assignment-sensitive certificate size and every source-law or support access in the computational model.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5 and Lemma 3 on page 8, reduce a connected ordinary \(Q[S]\) target to one intervention and a hedge-hitting problem; Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies their exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies their general-target Algorithm 3. Those results optimize ordinary intervention sets under fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics, not oracle-explicit SELECT-RAND-CTF-RAND-READ protocols with reusable counterfactual slices and branch-labelled certificates.
statements.consumer: Park and Lee's counterfactual structural causal bandit can compare the exact acquisition prices of finite reward-law protocols without treating source support as free hidden input.

statements.statement: Exactly one alternative holds for the oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\): either the feasible-case theorem returns \(E^{\star}\), or \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\). The latter occurs if and only if \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=0\) for every uniform certificate of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\). Exhaustive enumeration decides the alternative in time \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), with one cached source-oracle reply per queried distinct protocol; there is no certificate or output-length term in the infeasible input.
statements.justification: The explicit finite alternative makes infeasibility decidable without a polynomial-witness or full-incidence-compilation premise.
statements.gap: Fixed-source CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) decides one supplied collection; it does not decide existence over all priced legal physical protocols while charging access to their support and source-law handles.
statements.consumer: A planner can distinguish a costly but attainable reward-law query from one unattainable under the available catalogue.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\), translate its target \(Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)\) to \(Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0)\). For every \(t\ge1\) and every ordinary identifying collection \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\), quantify the complete finite source data \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}=\{Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\) and labels \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}=\{\ell_{i,b}:i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\). The protocols \(S_{B_i}\) are legal SELECT-RAND-READ protocols with every \(\rho_v\), their slices equal the corresponding ordinary kernels \(Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B_i)\), and the explicitly constructed uniform record list \(E_{\mathbf B}\), whose ownership masks cover every \(j\in[k]\), satisfies \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E_{\mathbf B};G)=1\) and \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathbf B})=\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\), with the outer sum over distinct sets. Conversely, for every accepted finite \(E\) in \(\iota(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}})\), augment each protocol by missing zero-cost READ records and take the distinct RAND-endpoint sets \(\mathbf B(E)\); their full assignments generate exactly the ordinary family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E)}\), which identifies \(Q[S_0](\cdot;x_0)\), and \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)=\sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E)}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\). Thus ordinary and embedded feasibility agree in both directions and their optimum costs are equal. Restricted to this image, the physical acquisition problem is exactly the 2025 JMLR ordinary intervention-design object with its fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics, so its ordinary complexity and approximation guarantees transfer only on that image; outside the image, CTF-RAND actions, partial child effects, reusable slices, precedence, conflicts, and the charged source-support interface are additional objects. In the 2025 JMLR article, Theorem 1 on page 5 supplies the singleton reduction for a c-component target, Lemma 3 on page 8 supplies the minimum-weight hedge-hitting equivalence, Theorems 2 and 3 on pages 6--7 give polynomial reductions from weighted vertex cover and minimum-weight hitting set, Corollaries 1 and 2 on pages 7--8 give NP-completeness and logarithmic inapproximability, Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies the general-target exact Algorithm 3.
statements.justification: The two-way embedding matches the ordinary \(Q[S]\) target and source-family semantics before certifying legality, acceptance, and exact cost preservation.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5, Lemma 3 on page 8, Lemma 7 on page 12, and Proposition 3 on page 16 concern ordinary intervention collections and their fixed \(Q[S]\) source families. They do not prove the two-way Layer-2.5 translation with explicit oracle-returned support, finite assignment labels, adequate READ records, complete-run acceptance, and exact protocol-cost preservation established here.
statements.consumer: The equivalence transfers the ordinary hardness frontier without silently enlarging the source family or changing the causal query.

statements.statement: As an already-known weighted-set-cover corollary, on \(\mathfrak C_{1}\) acquisition is exactly weighted set cover on the \(k\) factor identifiers, and the standard weighted greedy algorithm returns a legal certificate \(E_{\mathrm{gr}}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{gr}})\le H_k\operatorname{Opt}\). This imports the ordinary cover guarantee and makes no independent novelty claim.
statements.justification: This inherited corollary records the sole regime in which the familiar harmonic cover guarantee is valid and prevents it from being attributed to the general physical protocol problem.
statements.gap: There is no claimed novelty relative to Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025): Lemma 3 on page 8 is the minimum-weight hedge-hitting equivalence, the approximation discussion on page 12 applies greedy minimum-weight hitting set, and Corollary 2 on pages 7--8 records logarithmic inapproximability. The present corollary merely marks the physical restrictions under which that already-known cover logic applies.
statements.consumer: Experiment planners with isolated single-assay protocols obtain the familiar harmonic approximation without extrapolating it to protocols with shared-source synergy.

statements.statement: Set \(\varepsilon=1/10\). In each model let \(U_X,U_A,U_B,U_C\) be independent fair bits and let \(E_Y,E_Z\) be independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)\) bits independent of them. The structural equations are \(M_1:X=U_X,\ Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_B)\oplus E_Y,\ Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_C)\oplus E_Z\), and \(M_2:X=U_X,\ Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_C)\oplus E_Y,\ Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_A)\oplus E_Z\). Both are positive binary SCMs compatible with \(X\to Y\), \(X\to Z\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow Z\). For every one of the \(27\) regimes \(r\in\{\mathrm{natural},0,1\}^{\{X,Y,Z\}}\), conditional on any natural or fixed value of \(X\), the unfixed \(Y\) and \(Z\) are independent fair bits in both models. Thus, for \(a=(a_X,a_Y,a_Z)\), both regime laws equal \(p_r(a)=\prod_{W:r_W\ne\mathrm{natural}}\mathbf1\{a_W=r_W\}\prod_{W:r_W=\mathrm{natural}}(1/2)\), which covers all simultaneous interventions on any subset of \(\{X,Y,Z\}\). Nevertheless \(P_{M_1}(Y_0=1,Z_1=1)=1/4\), while \(P_{M_2}(Y_0=1,Z_1=1)=\tfrac12((9/10)^2+(1/10)^2)=41/100\). In \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sep}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\), SELECT \(s\) and all READs cost zero, each edge-specific CTF-RAND action costs one, and precedence is SELECT, then CTF-RAND, then READ, with no conflicts. The legal protocol \(S_{\mathrm{ind}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\) costs one, and its positive natural-\(X=1\) slice obeys \(P(Y=1,Z=1\mid X=1,S_{\mathrm{ind}})=P(Y_0=1,Z_1=1)\). The direct legal protocol \(S_{\mathrm{dir}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\) exposes the same joint without conditioning and costs two.
statements.justification: The explicit response-bit coupling proves ordinary observational equivalence, the cross-world gap, and the one-versus-two physical acquisition cost in one auditable witness.
statements.gap: Counterfactual realizability supplies the action semantics but not a positive binary pair with all 27 ordinary regime laws computed and a strict protocol-cost comparison.
statements.consumer: The witness is a complete regression fixture for the optimizer and certifies that the richer protocol class has genuine economic value.

sampling_model.design: The certificate-independent structural input fixes the legal action catalogue and costs and supplies the explicitly charged source oracle. Each selected protocol runs independently on fresh units; a distinct protocol is charged once, its law handle and exact support table are returned once, and all positive labelled slices are reusable.
sampling_model.units: Each SELECT draws a fresh independent unit from the target population, and all potential responses for that unit are generated by one recursive finite-discrete SCM compatible with \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: RAND actions replace a node mechanism for all affected children, while CTF-RAND actions fix the value delivered to their catalogued child subset without erasing the unit's natural decision.
sampling_model.overlap: For a legal protocol \(S\), positivity is required exactly for each used event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\), and is decided from the exact support bit table returned by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\). Events with unrecorded endpoints, uncatalogued assignments, conflicting values, or zero support are inadmissible; unused cells are unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None is required for the symbolic theorem. The source oracle returns an opaque complete-law handle and exact finite support, and every query and answer bit is charged; scalar-functional evaluation and empirical law estimation remain outside scope.

tldr: A finite physical catalogue can contain many legal Layer-2.5 acquisitions, but a computational claim must expose the source laws and exact support tests. The instance is therefore a certificate-independent structural string paired with a precisely charged oracle returning one immutable complete-law handle and finite support table per queried protocol. Operational acceptance performs every positivity test from that table and runs complete CTFIDU\({}^{+}\). The load-bearing theorem places one selected source and restriction schema outside all assignment and equality-type branches of each target district, giving at most \(k\) source-slice records and a polynomial certificate bound. This yields an exact, explicitly exponential minimum-cost optimizer and infeasibility decision, a static fixed-factor obstruction, a two-way ordinary \(Q[S]\) embedding, and a positive binary cost-one-versus-two CTF-RAND separation. The sharp complexity of searching an unrestricted source oracle is the first-class open question; bounded-treewidth compilation is not claimed.

project_justification.gap: Complete counterfactual identification fixes its source collection in advance, physical realizability treats one source law at a time, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025) optimize ordinary intervention objects under fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics. None supplies an operational cost problem that charges source-law and support access or resolves assignment-sensitive source switching.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a certificate-independent physical interface with explicit source support, a uniform factorwise acceptance witness, and an exact cost frontier whose computational accounting includes every source-oracle reply.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a charged source oracle, operational complete-run acceptance, a uniform one-source-per-factor theorem and polynomial certificate bound, exact finite optimization with an infeasibility alternative, a fixed-factor obstruction, an exact ordinary-source embedding, and a fully specified positive physical separation.

related_work: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025) define SELECT, RAND, CTF-RAND, and READ and prove CTF-REALIZE complete for physical sampling; their result determines realizability, not a minimum-cost collection or a charged source-support interface. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026) prove CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) complete for a fixed collection of Layer-3 inputs; Algorithm 2 and Appendix E motivate the uniform-normalization proof but do not exchange source choice across value assignments and equality types. Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021) provide unnesting and ctf-factorization from fixed sources. Kivva et al. (2022) establish positivity-sensitive generalized identification, while the exact event-level slice positivity here is a novel physical input restriction and is checked only through the explicit support oracle. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5, reduce a c-component target to one ordinary intervention; Lemma 3 on page 8 gives its minimum-weight hedge-hitting formulation; Theorems 2 and 3 on pages 6--7 and Corollaries 1 and 2 on pages 7--8 establish NP-completeness and logarithmic inapproximability; Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies exact Algorithm 2; and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies exact Algorithm 3 for a general target. The ordinary-subclass theorem matches that ordinary \(Q[S]\) object and fixed source-family semantics exactly. The general physical object instead permits edge-specific CTF-RAND actions, READ-dependent slices, and cost reuse, and proves a compact uniform factor certificate, while computational optimization remains finite exhaustive under the charged oracle. The familiar \(H_k\) guarantee is retained solely as the already-known weighted-cover corollary under three explicitly novel restricted-subclass conditions. Elahi et al. (2024) accelerate ordinary proxy experiment design without physical counterfactual actions. Courcelle and Mosbah (1993) and Arnborg, Lagergren, and Seese (1991) require a finite local relational predicate; an arbitrary source-support oracle is not silently treated as such, so no bounded-treewidth compiler or fixed-parameter runtime is claimed. Park and Lee (2026) supply the downstream counterfactual bandit setting, not an acquisition-cost theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The uniform source-choice theorem is the load-bearing target: failure on any finite assignment or equality pattern falsifies the polynomial certificate and exact optimizer as stated. The source oracle may return exponentially long support tables, all charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\), and exhaustive certificate search remains exponential in \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\). A bounded-treewidth compiler requires a separately justified local representation of oracle answers and lies outside the claimed kernel. The measured-ancestry rule rejects \(\operatorname{READ}(Y)\) alone for natural \(X\to Y\) whenever \(X\) is required, and rejects any unrecorded required natural parent or mediator. Physical slice positivity rejects exactly a used RAND, CTF-RAND, and ancestral READ conjunction having zero support.
honest_scope: The uniform one-source-per-factor equivalence, its canonical certificate bound, and the exact oracle-backed cost frontier are theorem targets; the oracle-query complexity frontier is open. Measured ancestry and positive admissible source events are novel physical restrictions. The source interface makes every law handle, support table, positivity decision, query, and answer explicit and charged. The one-action, protocolwise-legality, and factorwise-no-synergy conditions are novel restricted-subclass assumptions justified by isolated single-assay platforms; they are not attributed to ordinary design theory. The project claims neither a full-incidence compiler nor a treewidth bound, a scalar identifying-functional output, efficient numerical evaluation, compactness, conditional-query completeness, arbitrary partial-read completeness, mediator-depth fixed-parameter tractability, polynomial lower certificates, nor a global approximation ratio. General identifying expressions, support tables, search traces, and infeasibility certificates may be exponential.

seed_details.destination_search: Searches for bounded-treewidth causal experiment design found only generic MSO metatheorems and causal-graph special cases; none charges action, conflict, precedence, ownership, and value-request incidence to the width.
seed_details.red_team: A routine invocation of Courcelle's theorem after encoding the problem in MSO.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nonroutine result is the cost-preserving local interpretation: precomputing regimes or reachability can enumerate protocols or densify the structure and invalidate the claimed width.
seed_details.drop_reason: The charged source-support oracle is not an extensional bag-local relation, so invoking weighted MSO would hide a load-bearing representation assumption.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Make the equality constraints in the canonical-SCM endpoint program endogenous to the selected physical slices, then prove endpoint validity after data-dependent protocol choice.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for budgeted Layer-3 bounds and counterfactual source acquisition found fixed-source bounds and binary exact-identification design, but no joint selection-and-sharpness theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A mixed-integer wrapper around the published canonical-SCM polynomial program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Protocol selection changes the feasible equality system with complementarities, and a publishable version would require a sharp optimization and inference frontier rather than a wrapper.
seed_details.drop_reason: The sharp endpoint problem and post-selection inference form a second paper and do not share the finite obstruction certificate that makes the exact-identification kernel tractable.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace armwise feedback after CTF-POMIS pruning by confidence propagation through several identified factor maps supplied by one persistent acquired protocol.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for reusable acquisition costs in counterfactual structural causal bandits found action-space pruning and fixed-source fusion, but no persistent protocol-purchase benchmark.
seed_details.red_team: A bandit with side observations or a combinatorial semi-bandit after relabelling protocols as arms.
seed_details.rebuttal: The side-observation graph is itself induced by causal identification and shared counterfactual slices, but proving its statistical propagation requires a separate online theory.

seed_details.question: Does the one-action no-synergy restriction reduce the physical objective to the already-known weighted-set-cover case?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Verify the subclass reduction to a fixed protocol-to-factor incidence system, then invoke the published ordinary weighted-set-cover argument.
seed_details.destination_search: The ordinary design literature already supplies the harmonic weighted-set-cover guarantee; only its narrow applicability boundary is retained here.
seed_details.rebuttal: The weighted-set-cover conclusion is already known and is retained only to mark its valid boundary: it applies when each independently legal one-action protocol has a fixed factor coverage set, whereas general protocols can have precedence, conflict, and within-protocol synergy.

threads: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026) prove soundness and completeness of CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) for a fixed collection of Layer-3 input distributions. Algorithm 2 factors the query and searches the given regimes; it neither selects physical acquisitions nor prices shared slices.

Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025) prove CTF-REALIZE sound and complete under explicit physical actions and the one-use-per-mechanism constraint. The proof is an induction over a topological order that checks action compatibility, not a cost optimization.

Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022) give singleton reduction in Theorem 1, hedge hitting in Lemma 3, and NP-hardness in Theorem 2 for ordinary Layer-2 minimum-cost identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025) retain ordinary intervention objects and fixed ordinary source families while developing ordinary complexity and approximation results. Neither object owns several reusable Layer-2.5 slices or supplies a certificate-independent charged source-law and support interface.

Elahi et al. (2024) provide faster weighted Max-SAT and integer-programming formulations for the same ordinary proxy-experiment setting; this occupies solver reformulation alone, not the physical counterfactual certificate kernel.
literature_map.occupancy_check: No located result combines a charged source-law/support interface, uniform factorwise CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) certificates, physical protocol cost reuse, and an exact ordinary-source embedding.

threads: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021) prove counterfactual unnesting, ancestral factorization, and complete ctfID from fixed observational and experimental sources; the factors are concrete counterfactual events rather than symbolic acquisition certificates.

Kivva et al. (2022) show that positivity is essential for sound generalized identification and replace an invalid cross-source argument by positivity-aware reduction to classical identification subproblems.

Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026), Appendix E, establish necessity factor by factor and use ctf-thickets for joint failure across fixed input regimes, but do not exchange source choice with free ancestral assignments or bound paid slice references by the factor count.
Correa and Bareinboim (2025) give complete counterfactual graphical separation and ctf-calculus machinery, but no acquisition normal form.
literature_map.occupancy_check: The exact source-choice and free-assignment quantifier exchange, together with the polynomial transcript bound, is not stated in adjacent complete-identification papers.

threads: Courcelle and Mosbah (1993), Sections 3 and 4.7--4.8, compute weighted monadic-second-order extrema bottom-up on bounded-width decomposition terms.
Arnborg, Lagergren, and Seese (1991) establish extended-MSO optimization on fixed bounded-treewidth graph classes.
Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022), Theorem 2, establishes unrestricted NP-hardness, while their tractable cases use restrictive causal-graph geometries.
The full-incidence search found no causal-design theorem whose width includes catalogue actions, conflicts, precedence, ownership, and value requests.
literature_map.occupancy_check: Generic metatheorems do not accept an arbitrary charged source oracle as a local extensional relation; a separate representation theorem is required.
